div.head: IV Atr 5
div.ab: Etiam dixerunt, quod nichil eis interesse uidebatur inter falsarios et mercatores qui bonam pecuniam portant ad falsarios et ab ipsis emunt, ut inpurum et minus appendens operentur, et inde mangonant et barganiant, et eos etiam qui conos faciunt in occultis et uendunt falsariis pro pecunia et incidunt alterius monetarii nomen in eo, et non ipsius immundi.

Etiam dixerunt quod nichil eis interesse videbatur inter falsarios et mercatores qui bonam pecuniam portant ad falsarios et ab ipsis emunt ut inpurum et minus appendens operentur, et inde mangonant et barganiant, et eos etiam qui conos faciunt in occultis et vendunt falsariis pro pecunia et incidunt alterius monetarii nomen in eo et non ipsius immundi.

Ferner haben sie bestimmt, dass ihnen kein Unterschied zu sein scheine zwischen [erstens Münz-]fälschern und [zweitens solchen] Kaufleuten, die gutes Geld zu Fälschern hintragen und von diesen bestechend erlangen, dass letztere unreines und weniger vollwichtiges [in erhöhter Anzahl Münzen] herstellen, und mit diesem [schlechten Geld] handeln und einkaufen, und ferner [drittens] denen, welche verstohlen [Münz]stempel anfertigen und den Fälschern gegen Geld verkaufen, indem sie den Namen eines anderen [unschuldigen] Münzers, und nicht dieses schuldigen [Bestellers], darin eingraviren.

Further they have determined that there seems to them to be no difference between [first] forgers [of coin] and [second, those] merchants who take good money to forgers and by bribery get them to produce impure and underweight [coin, in greater numbers], and trade and buy with this [bad money]; and [third] those who secretly make [coin-]dies and sell them to forgers for money, engraving on them the name of another [innocent] moneyer and not that of the guilty [customer].

Further, they have decided that no distinction is to be drawn between those who issue base coin, and traders who take good money to such men and bribe them to produce [from it] coin which is defective in quality and weight with which they trade and buy, and, thirdly, those who make dies in secret and sell them to coiners for money, engraving upon them a name which is that of another moneyer and not that of the guilty one.
